messages:
alex: quick follow-up to the GQA/MQA kernel selection RFC — saw a case where the cost model prefers the grouped-query kernel but end-to-end p99 increases.
alex: TL;DR: group-kernel wins on token-cost but loses on per-query overhead when query-length variance > ~4x.
alex: pasted a small repro from perf lab below, can folks sanity-check?

```
# perf snapshot: 8k requests, mixed query lengths
policy: grouped-query (k=32)
avg_tokens: 42    avg_q_len: 18   var_q_len: 82
throughput: 18k tok/s  p50: 38ms  p95: 210ms  p99: 380ms
cpu-steal spikes during short queries

policy: multi-query (k=8)
throughput: 16.5k tok/s p50: 48ms p95: 160ms p99: 230ms
cost_estimate: group < multi by 12% (token model only)
```

alex: the issue looks like fixed-per-query setup + KV cache warmup per grouped batch causing short queries to wait.
ying: can you paste the exact input distribution? curious how many 2-8 token queries vs 100+ tokens.
alex: split roughly: 62% short (2-10), 30% medium (11-80), 8% long (>80). created a synthetic with same mix.
priya: thanks. that distribution will bias group kernels toward batching more short queries with long ones, which hurts tail for shorts.
priya: suggestion: add a per-query overhead term to the cost model: cost = token_cost + alpha * q_count_per_batch + beta * kv_warmups
priya: where alpha is measured from the runtime (scheduling + prefetch) and beta penalizes mixing long+short in same group.
sam: i like measuring alpha/beta from microbenchmarks rather than heuristics. we should instrument: time_to_first_token vs per_token_time by q_len and batch_size.
sam: propose a small benchmark harness + a lightweight profiler counter for "kv_warmup_bytes".
ying: +1. also consider a quick heuristic: if median_q_len < 8 and 90p_len > 64, disallow mixing (i.e., split groups by quantized length buckets).
priya: splitting buckets is simple and low-risk. downside: may reduce overall token-efficiency for heavy-medium tails.
alex: what about an adaptive policy: start with token-cost-driven selection, observe p95 drift, then flip to tail-aware selection for that route for N minutes.
sam: that fits our rollout model. canary on low-traffic routes first.
priya: one implementation detail: kernel selector currently receives only aggregate stats (avg_len, batch_size). we'll need to extend selector proto to include q_len_histogram or at least median and 90p.
alex: agreed — small proto bump: add median_q_len and q90_len (integers). selector can fallback to avg if missing.
ying: I'd also like an offline simulator to run the cost model across traces. we can iterate on alpha/beta quickly.
alex: action items:
- sam: add microbench harness + kv_warmup metric (ETA 3d)
- priya: draft cost-model update with alpha/beta and bucket-split heuristic (ETA 2d)
- ying: offline simulator using existing traces (ETA 4d)
- alex: create canary config and rollout plan (ETA 1d)

runtime-bot: deployment pipeline triggered: branch gqa-mqa-cost-model-update -> canary cluster (id: can-42)
runtime-bot: build 0.47.3 passed unit tests, running perf benchmarks

ying: nice, thanks all. ping me when harness results land in the perf dashboard :eyes:
alex: thanks — will post numbers and a short RFC follow-up with proto change tomorrow. :thumbsup:
sam: will run the canary during low-traffic window and collect p99 samples.
priya: noted. if we see regressions we rollback to token-only selection quickly. :ok_hand:
